newsitem.title: USA: Union Texas Petroleum sets $229 mln budget.
newsitem.headline: Union Texas Petroleum sets $229 mln budget.

text.p: Union Texas Petroleum said its board of directors have approved a 1997 capital spending budget of $229 million, up 23 percent from year-ago levels.
The larger budget reflects increased spending in the company's worldwide exploration activities and its petrochemical business in Louisiana.

The exploration budget, which is nearly 90 percent above last year's, will focus on drilling and seismic activity in Italy, Tunisia and Alaska and other areas in Latin America, Africa, the Middle East and Central Asia.
Union Texas also said it will participate in exploration programs in the United Kingdom, Indonesia and Pakistan.
It said the exploration program will focus more on proven hydrocarbon basins, with less emphasis on frontier plays that had been pursued in the past several years.
The company cut development spending plans to about $127 million from last year's $150 million.
Union Texas said it plans to spend about $32 million on capital projects at its petrochemical operations in Louisiana, up from $8 million in 1996.
